paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: Mathematical problems across educational levels. We curate and categorize problems by difficulty and subject area.
model_annotation: This pie chart represents the distribution of mathematical problem categories across various educational levels. The chart contains twelve slices, each representing a different subject area or difficulty level. The largest slice, colored blue and representing “Algebra – High School,” occupies approximately 17.83% of the total area. Following this is “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” colored orange with approximately 9.56%, while “Geometry – Olympiad-level” colored green occupies about 6.46%. The remaining slices represent “Number Theory – Olympiad-level” colored yellow with 1.03%, “Probability – University-level” colored teal with 3.62%, “Differential Equations – University-level” colored purple with 6.20%, "Calculus and Analysis – University-level" colored pink with 4.39%, “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level” colored light blue with 2.5%, "Pre-Calculus – High School" colored dark blue with 14.21%, “Algebra – Olympiad-level” colored red with 21.19%, “Geometry – High School” colored brown with 1.4%, “Statistics – University-level” colored grey with 17%, and “Algebra” colored black with 82%.  A legend is present, indicating the color-to-category mapping, and percentage labels are displayed within each slice. The slices appear to be arranged in descending order of size, from largest to smallest.
